newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa-UAP says Simco to buy CIPM and merge.
newsitem.headline: Axa-UAP says Simco to buy CIPM and merge.

text.p: French insurer Axa SA-UAP said on Thursday it planned to sell 65 percent of CIPM property group to Simco, which is 36 percent-owned by the Axa-UAP group, and this would be followed by a merger of CIPM into Simco.

Axa-UAP said in a statement that the deal would reduce its real estate exposure by around six billion francs, improve its asset allocation and allow it to be involved in "a sizeable European listed real estate holding company with a large float."
It said the transaction would take place in three steps. SIMCO would buy 65 percent of CIPM's shares for 3.9 billion francs in cash, or 218 francs per share.
Simco would then make a simplified public tender on the CIPM shares not owned by Axa-UAP at 243 francs per share.
This would be followed by a merger of CIPM into Simco at an exchange ratio of two Simco shares for five CIPM shares.

Simco is the largest real estate holding company on the Paris market, with 707,000 square metres of mainly residential property. CIPM is the second largest, with 523,000 square metres of almost exclusively residential property under ownership or management, it said.
"Following the transaction, the Axa-UAP group will own approximately 49 percent of SIMCO," it said.
Axa-UAP said it would request exemption from the requirement to initiate a public tender offer for SIMCO.
